items.question: What happens when a file has no Feature: line, such as an empty file?
items.ticket: raise a clear error on invalid files
items.chose: Throws a ParseError at line 1 saying the Feature line is missing.
items.instead: Return an empty feature, or report the error at the last line of the file.

items.question: Is a feature with no scenarios valid?
items.ticket: Valid files return scenarios in order
items.chose: Returns the feature with an empty scenarios list and no error.
items.instead: Throw an error because the feature has no scenarios.

items.question: How are Scenario Outline, Examples and Rule handled?
items.chose: Throws a ParseError at that line saying the keyword is not supported.
items.instead: Parse them as scenarios or outlines, or skip them silently.

items.question: What happens to a step that appears before any Background or Scenario?
items.chose: Throws a ParseError at the step's line.
items.instead: Ignore the step, or attach it to the feature.

items.question: How is text that matches no known construct handled?
items.ticket: raise a clear error on invalid files
items.chose: In the feature header it is treated as a description and ignored. Inside a Background or Scenario it throws a ParseError at that line.

items.question: Which line is reported when tags are not followed by a Scenario?
items.ticket: Invalid files report the line of the error
items.chose: Reports the line of the tag line, not the line of the offending content after it. At end of file it also reports the tag line.
items.instead: Report the line of the unexpected line that follows the tags.

items.question: Are tags returned, and what form do they take?
items.chose: Collects tags from preceding tag lines onto the scenario as strings that keep the '@'. Tags on the Feature line are discarded.
items.instead: Strip the '@', or keep feature-level tags and apply them to scenarios.

items.question: Is the Background returned, and are its steps kept separate from scenario steps?
items.chose: Returns the background steps separately (null if there is none), and a second Background or one after a Scenario is an error.
items.instead: Prepend background steps to every scenario, or allow a late Background.

items.question: How are doc strings and data tables handled, and can they be combined on one step?
items.chose: Attaches a doc string as an array of lines with the opening indent stripped. Attaches a table as rows of trimmed cells. A step can't have both, and an unclosed doc string is an error at the line that opened it.
items.instead: Join the doc string into one string, ignore tables and doc strings, or allow both on one step.

items.question: Does a step keyword need whitespace after it, and what does a bare keyword mean?
items.chose: Requires whitespace or end of line after the keyword. A bare keyword gives an empty step text, and 'Givenx' is an unrecognised line.
items.instead: Reject a step with empty text, or accept a keyword with no space after it.

items.question: How are comments, blank lines, CRLF endings and a byte order mark treated?
items.chose: Skips blank lines and lines starting with '#', strips '\r' and a leading BOM, and keeps original line numbers. Inside doc strings, '#' lines are content.
items.instead: Treat '#' lines as errors, or fail on a BOM.

items.question: Does a Scenario keep its original line number, and are 'Example:' and 'Scenario:' both accepted?
items.chose: Records the 1-based line of the Scenario or Example keyword line. Both keywords are treated as scenarios.
items.instead: Accept only 'Scenario:', or record the line of the first tag.
